fcff_cash_flow.label: Base-year FCFF
fcff_cash_flow.help: Annual free cash flow to the firm, before financing. Discount at WACC; do not substitute FCFE.

fcfe_cash_flow.label: Base-year FCFE
fcfe_cash_flow.help: Annual free cash flow to common equity, after financing and net borrowing. Discount at cost of equity; do not subtract debt again.

price.label: Share price
price.help: Last saved market quote or your manual reference. Refresh online to request the latest available PSE EDGE quote; it may be delayed. Offline calculations use the saved value.

shares.label: Number of common shares
shares.help: Outstanding common shares, available on the PSE EDGE stock-data page or in the share-capital note. Enter the full count, without converting to millions. Use the appropriate diluted count if your valuation includes dilution.

cash_flow.label: Annual cash available to the business
cash_flow.help: Find the annual cash-flow statement and income statement. This is calculated, not usually a printed total: operating profit × (1 − tax rate) + depreciation − spending on equipment − increase in working capital. It is called free cash flow to the firm (FCFF). Do not substitute net profit or cash from operations alone.

growth.label: Expected yearly cash growth
growth.help: An assumption for the next five years, not a reported figure. 3% is an illustrative starting point; compare several years of recurring cash flows and the company's outlook. Higher growth raises the estimate.

discount_rate.label: Required yearly return
discount_rate.help: The return used to translate future money into today's value. For business cash flow, use the weighted cost of debt and shareholder funding (WACC). For dividends or shareholder cash flow, use shareholders' required return. The calculator below shows how a starting estimate is built.

terminal_growth.label: Growth after year 5
terminal_growth.help: A long-run assumption used after the five-year forecast. 2% is an illustrative conservative starting point, not company guidance. It must be lower than Required yearly return. Small changes can greatly affect value.

net_debt.label: Debt minus available cash
net_debt.help: Calculate interest-bearing borrowings minus excess/available cash, plus any other claims owed ahead of common shareholders. Find borrowings and cash in the balance sheet and notes. Total liabilities is not the same as debt. Do not subtract cash the business needs to operate without reviewing it.

dividend.label: Annual dividend per share
dividend.help: Recurring cash dividends per common share over a year. Find declarations on PSE EDGE's Dividends and Rights page. Exclude one-off special dividends when projecting a permanent payout.

eps.label: Earnings per share (EPS)
eps.help: Profit attributable to common shareholders divided by the weighted-average common shares. PSE EDGE shows basic and diluted EPS. Use annual or trailing-12-month EPS, not one quarter's EPS. Current P/E = Share price ÷ Earnings per share.

bvps.label: Book value per share
bvps.help: Common shareholders' accounting equity divided by common shares. PSE EDGE usually displays it. Current P/B = Share price ÷ Book value per share. Accounting book value is not necessarily market value.

multiple.label: Comparison ratio
multiple.help: A valuation benchmark, separate from the company's current ratio. For P/E, compare annual EPS with suitable companies' P/E ratios or the company's history. Using the current P/E simply reproduces the current share price. A saved benchmark is an assumption you can change, not a guaranteed fair ratio.

roe.label: Sustainable return on equity
roe.help: Forward sustainable common ROE, not necessarily the latest reported ROE.

payout.label: Earnings payout ratio
payout.help: Share of earnings distributed; retained earnings grow book value.

asset_value.label: Value of owned assets and businesses
asset_value.help: For a holding company such as AC, add the value of each business multiplied by the ownership percentage. This is a sum-of-parts estimate, not the consolidated Total Assets line. Subsidiary equity values already reflect their own debt. Use the investment/subsidiary notes and a component-by-component calculation.

liabilities.label: Remaining parent-company debt and claims
liabilities.help: For sum-of-parts, subtract parent-company obligations not already deducted from business values. Check the parent-only balance sheet and borrowing notes. Do not subtract the group's consolidated liabilities again. This requires a reviewed calculation; the app cannot infer it from Total Liabilities.

discount.label: Discount to asset-based value
discount.help: A chosen reduction for holding-company costs, complexity or uncertainty. 0% means no discount. A 15% starting discount is illustrative, not a required accounting adjustment or industry average. Compare 0%, 15% and 25% and explain your choice.

affo_per_share.label: Annual AFFO per share
affo_per_share.help: Reviewed recurring adjusted funds from operations per common share.

required_yield.label: Required dividend yield
required_yield.help: Required sustainable yield, including relevant risk premium.

noi.label: Annual net operating income
noi.help: Stabilized attributable property NOI before financing.

in_force_value.label: Value of in-force business
in_force_value.help: Present value from reviewed actuarial assumptions; not total premiums.

operating_profit.label: Annual operating profit
operating_profit.help: Income statement: profit/income from operations, before financing and tax.

depreciation.label: Annual depreciation and amortization
depreciation.help: Cash-flow statement: non-cash depreciation and amortization added back to profit.

capital_spending.label: Annual equipment and property spending
capital_spending.help: Cash-flow statement investing activities: purchases of property, plant and equipment. Enter spending as positive.

working_capital_increase.label: Annual increase in operating working capital
working_capital_increase.help: Increase in operating receivables and inventory minus increase in operating payables. Exclude cash and financing debt. A decrease is negative.

operating_cash_flow.label: Cash from operating activities
operating_cash_flow.help: Cash-flow statement: net cash generated from operating activities. This alone is not business free cash flow.

debt.label: Interest-bearing debt
debt.help: Borrowing notes: current plus long-term interest-bearing borrowings, including relevant leases. Do not use total liabilities.

cash.label: Cash available to offset debt
cash.help: Balance sheet cash and cash equivalents, adjusted to exclude restricted cash or cash needed for operations when appropriate.

additional_capex.label: Other capital investment
additional_capex.help: Include capitalized software, intangibles and other investment not already in equipment/property spending. Enter positive spending, or an explicitly reviewed zero.

other_claims.label: Other claims ahead of common shareholders
other_claims.help: Include preferred equity, non-controlling interests when cash flows consolidate subsidiaries, and other claims not already in debt. Review values and avoid double counting. Enter zero only after checking.

other_working_capital_change.label: Other operating working-capital increase
other_working_capital_change.help: Net change in other operating assets minus other operating liabilities, excluding cash and financing debt. Adjust acquisitions, FX and reclassifications. Zero means reviewed and not material.

other_noncash.label: Other non-cash operating adjustments
other_noncash.help: Non-cash operating charges to add back, net of non-cash gains to subtract, beyond depreciation. Exclude financing items. Enter zero only after review.

receivables.label: Current year: Operating trade receivables
receivables.help: Use comparable annual balance-sheet closing balances. Exclude financing items. Include other operating working-capital movements separately when material.

previous_receivables.label: Previous year: Operating trade receivables
previous_receivables.help: Use comparable annual balance-sheet closing balances. Exclude financing items. Include other operating working-capital movements separately when material.

inventory.label: Current year: Inventory
inventory.help: Use comparable annual balance-sheet closing balances. Exclude financing items. Include other operating working-capital movements separately when material.

previous_inventory.label: Previous year: Inventory
previous_inventory.help: Use comparable annual balance-sheet closing balances. Exclude financing items. Include other operating working-capital movements separately when material.

payables.label: Current year: Operating trade payables
payables.help: Use comparable annual balance-sheet closing balances. Exclude financing items. Include other operating working-capital movements separately when material.

previous_payables.label: Previous year: Operating trade payables
previous_payables.help: Use comparable annual balance-sheet closing balances. Exclude financing items. Include other operating working-capital movements separately when material.

dcf_fcff.name: DCF · enterprise cash flow
dcf_fcff.description: Cash-flow valuation estimates five years of cash the business can generate, adds its continuing value, and converts that future cash into today's money. Subtract Debt minus available cash, then divide by Number of common shares. It is useful when operating cash generation can be forecast. FCFF means business cash before financing; WACC means the blended return required by lenders and shareholders.

dcf_fcfe.name: DCF · equity cash flow
dcf_fcfe.description: Shareholder cash-flow valuation discounts cash remaining for common shareholders after financing. Use shareholders' required return. Debt is already reflected in these cash flows, so do not subtract it again. FCFE means free cash flow to equity.

ddm.name: Dividend discount model
ddm.description: Dividend valuation estimates a share's value from sustainable future dividends. Fair value = Annual dividend per share × (1 + Long-run dividend growth) ÷ (Required yearly return − Long-run dividend growth). It fits stable dividend payers. It is less useful when payouts are irregular or not supported by earnings and cash.

pe.name: Normalized P/E
pe.description: Earnings valuation asks what one share could be worth if investors paid a chosen comparison P/E for its annual earnings. Fair value = Earnings per share × Comparison P/E. It is useful for profitable businesses with reasonably stable earnings. Current P/E measures today's market pricing; it is not an independent fair-value benchmark.

pb.name: Relative P/B
pb.description: Book-value valuation compares share price with the accounting equity behind each share. Fair value = Book value per share × Comparison P/B. It can be useful for banks and other asset-based businesses, but asset quality and profitability matter. A low current P/B alone does not prove undervaluation.

justified_pb.name: Justified P/B
justified_pb.description: Connects sustainable ROE, growth and cost of equity.

residual_income.name: Residual income
residual_income.description: Book value plus five years of excess returns and continuing residual income.

sotp.name: Sum of the parts
sotp.description: Sum-of-parts values a holding company by adding its ownership share of each business, subtracting remaining parent obligations and applying any chosen holding-company discount. It is useful for companies such as AC whose businesses have different economics. The required business values are estimates, not one figure copied from consolidated Total Assets.

rnav.name: Revalued net asset value
rnav.description: Revalued net asset value uses estimated current values for properties and development projects, less obligations. It suits property businesses. It needs project/property valuations; the balance sheet's historical asset costs are not automatically current market values.

nav.name: Net asset value
nav.description: Net asset value estimates what belongs to common shareholders after subtracting obligations from reviewed asset values. Divide by shares, with any chosen discount. It suits asset-based businesses. Market-value NAV and accounting book value are different, so label the basis you use.

affo.name: P/AFFO
affo.description: Recurring AFFO per share multiplied by a selected valuation multiple.

dividend_cap.name: Dividend capitalization
dividend_cap.description: Dividend capitalization divides a sustainable annual dividend by the yield you would require. For example, PHP 3 at a 6% required yield implies PHP 50. It can help compare income-producing stocks such as REITs. The required yield is a risk judgment, not the current dividend yield copied back into the formula.

cap_rate.name: Property capitalization
cap_rate.description: Stabilized property NOI capitalized into asset value, less net claims.

embedded_value.name: Insurance embedded value
embedded_value.description: Adjusted net worth plus reviewed value of in-force business.

rate_help.risk_free: The saved 91-day Philippine Treasury-bill yield is a short-term project-policy proxy, not a duration-matched rate for a long-lived business. For long-term DCF, consider a dated PHP long-term government benchmark with any appropriate sovereign-risk adjustment. Keep currency, inflation basis and equity premium consistent. Record the source and date in your analysis notes; online stock refresh does not refresh this rate.
rate_help.beta: How sensitive the stock has historically been to market moves. 1 means roughly market-like sensitivity; above 1 means more; below 1 means less. The default 1 is an illustrative neutral assumption, not an estimated beta for this stock.
rate_help.premium: Extra return shareholders require above the government rate for equity risk. The starting 6% is an illustrative assumption, not a current official rate. Shareholders' required return = government rate + beta × this premium.
rate_help.debt_cost: Annual borrowing cost before tax. Estimate interest expense ÷ average interest-bearing debt, or use disclosed loan rates. The starting 7% is illustrative. Find interest expense and borrowing notes in the full annual report.
rate_help.tax: Tax rate applied to the interest deduction. The starting 25% is illustrative; actual company tax treatment, incentives and deductible interest may differ. Use the tax note to choose an appropriate rate.
rate_help.debt_weight: Debt as a share of debt plus equity funding: interest-bearing debt ÷ (interest-bearing debt + market value of equity). Market equity = Share price × Number of common shares. The starting 30% is illustrative unless calculated from reviewed inputs.

default_note: Illustrative modeling assumptions, not company forecasts. Review and confirm before calculating.
